title: Accuracy vs Precision
stem:
Two laboratory pH meters are compared. Meter 1 gives the true pH correctly in 85 out of 100 tests. Meter 2 gives the true pH correctly in 92 out of 100 tests. When each meter is used to re-test the same sample 50 times, Meter 1 returns the same reading 49 times and Meter 2 returns the same reading 42 times.

Which statement best compares the two meters?
answer_reason: Accuracy = how often the reading is correct. Meter 1 = 85%, Meter 2 = 92% — Meter 2 is more accurate. Precision = how consistent repeated readings are. Meter 1 = 49/50 = 98%, Meter 2 = 42/50 = 84% — Meter 1 is more precise. So Meter 2 is more accurate but Meter 1 is more precise.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Meter 1 is more accurate but Meter 2 is more precise.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Meter 2 is more accurate but Meter 1 is more precise.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Meter 2 is both more accurate and more precise.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Meter 1 is both more accurate and more precise.

title: Detentions Average
stem:
In a class of ten pupils, the average number of detentions per pupil this term is 3.6. Four pupils received three detentions each, three pupils received two detentions each, and one pupil received one detention. Of the remaining two pupils, Aisha received three more detentions than Ben.

How many detentions did Ben receive?
answer_reason: Total detentions = 10 × 3.6 = 36. Known detentions = (4 × 3) + (3 × 2) + 1 = 12 + 6 + 1 = 19. Aisha and Ben share 36 − 19 = 17 detentions. Aisha = Ben + 3, so Ben + (Ben + 3) = 17 ⇒ 2 × Ben = 14 ⇒ Ben = 7.

title: Conference Seating
stem:
Six delegates sit in a row of six chairs numbered 1 to 6 (left to right). Farah sits in chair 3. George sits immediately to the right of Farah. Hana sits in chair 1 or chair 6. Iqbal sits somewhere to the left of George but not in the chair directly next to Farah. Jasper and Kim take the remaining chairs. Kim does not sit directly next to Hana.

Which of the following seating arrangements, listed from chair 1 to chair 6, is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Farah = chair 3 and George = chair 4. Iqbal is left of George but not directly next to Farah, so Iqbal = chair 1 (chair 2 would be next to Farah). Hana is in chair 1 or 6; chair 1 is taken, so Hana = chair 6. Jasper and Kim take chairs 2 and 5. Kim cannot be directly next to Hana (chair 6), so Kim ≠ chair 5, meaning Kim = 2 and Jasper = 5. Order: Iqbal, Kim, Farah, George, Jasper, Hana — option B.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Iqbal, Jasper, Farah, George, Kim, Hana

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Iqbal, Kim, Farah, George, Jasper, Hana

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Jasper, Iqbal, Farah, George, Kim, Hana

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Hana, Iqbal, Farah, George, Jasper, Kim

title: Gym Class Attendance
stem: The table shows the number of attendees at four fitness classes over three months at a community gym.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Spin had the highest total attendance over the three months.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Spin totals 120 + 118 + 126 = 364. Yoga totals 286, Pilates 197, HIIT 173. Spin is the highest.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every class saw attendance rise between February and March.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Yoga 92→110, Spin 118→126, Pilates 65→72, HIIT 58→70. Every class grew from February to March.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: HIIT will attract more attendees than Yoga in April.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The data does not extend to April. Extrapolating future trends from past data is not supported.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Pilates attendance grew by more than 20 percent from January to March.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Pilates went from 60 to 72 — an increase of 12. 12 / 60 = 0.20, so the growth is exactly 20%, not more than 20%.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Spin attendance dropped between January and February.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Spin went from 120 in January to 118 in February — a drop of 2.

title: Airport Passenger Profile
stem:
The diagram categorises passengers passing through an airport terminal on a weekend. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a weekend arrival who is a frequent flyer with checked baggage but is not a minor travelling alone?
answer_reason: Weekend arrival is the outer category; every labelled passenger sits inside it. The question asks for a passenger inside weekend arrival, checked baggage, and frequent flyer, but outside minor alone. Letter P is inside weekend arrival only. Letter Q is inside weekend arrival and checked baggage but not frequent flyer. Letter R is inside weekend arrival and frequent flyer but not checked baggage. Letter T is inside weekend arrival and minor alone — includes minor alone, which is excluded. Letter S is inside weekend arrival, checked baggage, and frequent flyer, and outside minor alone — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter S.

title: Coloured Marbles
stem:
A bag contains 5 red marbles, 4 blue marbles and 3 green marbles. Two marbles are drawn at random, one after the other, without replacement.

What is the probability that both marbles are blue?
answer_reason: Total marbles = 12. P(first blue) = 4/12 = 1/3. After one blue is removed, 3 blues remain in 11 marbles. P(second blue | first blue) = 3/11. P(both blue) = (1/3) × (3/11) = 3/33 = 1/11.

title: Morning Shift Deliveries
stem:
A courier logs 90 deliveries one day. 42 are classed as priority, 35 are oversized, 30 fall within the morning shift window.

14 deliveries are both priority and oversized. 12 priority deliveries fall within the morning shift window. 10 oversized deliveries fall within the morning shift window. 6 deliveries are all three. 17 deliveries are none of these three.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 6 deliveries are in all three and 17 are outside. Scan — A shows 4 in the centre — eliminate A. B shows 22 outside — eliminate B. That leaves C and D. The stem says 14 are priority and oversized, and 6 of those are also morning shift, so priority-and-oversized only = 14 − 6 = 8. C shows 8 ✓. D shows 12 — eliminate D. Answer: C.

title: Exam Pipeline
stem:
The diagram shows candidates progressing through five stages of an exam pipeline: registered, screening, written test, oral test, and practical. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a candidate who reached the written test and the oral test, but not the practical and not any earlier stage?
answer_reason: Consecutive stages overlap in the diagram; non-consecutive stages do not. The question asks for the region inside the written test and the oral test but outside the practical and outside every earlier stage. Letter P is registered only. Letter Q is registered and at screening. Letter R is at screening and the written test — not the oral test. Letter S is at the written test and the oral test, and outside every other stage — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter S.

title: Commute Pipeline
stem:
160 commuters were surveyed on three legs of their morning commute: local train, tube, and office bus. No one takes the tube without also taking the local train, and no one takes the office bus without also taking the tube.

48 commuters took the local train only. 24 took both the local train and the tube but not the office bus. 18 took both the tube and the office bus. 52 took none of the three legs.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 52 took none of the three and 18 took office bus + tube + local train. Scan — B shows 45 outside — eliminate B. D shows 12 in the triple overlap — eliminate D. That leaves A and C. The stem says 18 took tube and office bus; all of those also took the local train (per the consecutive-legs rule) — so tube-and-office-bus-only = 18 − 18 = 0, and that region should be omitted. A has no tube-and-office-bus-only region ✓. C has a tube-and-office-bus-only region of 6, which would mean 6 commuters took the office bus without the local train — violates the consecutive rule. Eliminate C. Answer: A.

title: Bookshop Orders
stem:
An online bookshop processes 140 orders one week across three categories: gift-wrapped, dispatched by first-class post, and placed by members.

38 orders are gift-wrapped, 52 are dispatched by first-class post, and 60 are placed by members. 12 orders are both gift-wrapped and dispatched by first-class post. 22 orders are both dispatched by first-class post and placed by members. 14 orders are both gift-wrapped and placed by members. 6 orders fall into all three categories. 14 orders are none of the three.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 6 orders are in all three categories and 14 are outside. Scan — C shows 10 in the centre — eliminate C. D shows 20 outside — eliminate D. That leaves A and B. The stem says 12 orders are gift-wrapped and dispatched by first-class post; 6 of those are also members, so gift-wrapped-and-first-class only = 12 − 6 = 6. A shows 6 ✓. B shows 10 — eliminate B. Answer: A.

title: Rare Disease Test
stem:
A rare disease affects 1 in 2,000 adults. A screening test is 98% sensitive (correctly identifies 98% of people who have the disease) and 95% specific (correctly identifies 95% of people who do not have the disease).

If an adult from this population tests positive, roughly what is the probability they actually have the disease?
answer_reason: Imagine 100,000 adults: 50 have the disease, 99,950 do not. True positives ≈ 98% × 50 = 49. False positives = 5% × 99,950 ≈ 4,998. Total positives ≈ 5,047. P(disease | positive) ≈ 49 / 5,047 ≈ 1%. The high test accuracy does not overcome the very low base rate.

title: Hobby Club Membership
stem:
The diagram shows members of a hobby club categorised by five activities: chess, baking, hiking, pottery, and drama. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a member who takes part in baking and hiking but neither chess, pottery, nor drama?
answer_reason: Consecutive activities overlap in the diagram; non-consecutive activities do not, because no one takes a later activity without taking every earlier one. The question asks for the region inside baking and hiking but outside chess, pottery, and drama. Letter P sits inside chess only. Letter Q sits inside chess and baking — includes chess, which is excluded. Letter S sits inside hiking and pottery — includes pottery, which is excluded. Letter R sits inside baking and hiking, outside chess, pottery, and drama — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter R.

title: Later School Start
stem: Should secondary schools in the UK move the start of the school day from 08:45 to 10:00 to improve student academic performance?
answer_reason: B connects the action (later start) to the outcome (academic performance) with study evidence. A addresses preference, not performance. C addresses logistics, not performance. D assumes teaching quality is the only relevant factor and doesn't address whether a later start could still help.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; teenagers tend to get up late at the weekend, so they would prefer a later start.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; multiple controlled studies have shown that moving start times to after 09:30 increases average exam scores by around 4% in secondary-age students, directly improving academic performance.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; parents of younger children would need to rearrange school runs, causing logistical problems.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; academic performance depends on teaching quality, which a later start will not change.

title: Only Pilots
stem: Only qualified pilots may land at the private airstrip. Every qualified pilot has passed the medical review. Some people who have passed the medical review are instructors. No instructor uses the short runway.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Anyone who lands at the private airstrip has passed the medical review.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only qualified pilots may land there, and all qualified pilots have passed the medical review — so anyone landing has passed.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All instructors are qualified pilots.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premises say some people who passed the medical are instructors, not that all instructors are pilots. Instructors might not be pilots at all.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some qualified pilots are instructors.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: We know some medical-reviewed people are instructors, but those instructors are not guaranteed to be pilots — being a pilot is a stricter category.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No instructor may land at the private airstrip.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some instructors could also be qualified pilots — the premises do not forbid it, so we cannot rule out instructors landing.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every person who uses the short runway is not an instructor.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: No instructor uses the short runway, so everyone using it must be a non-instructor.

title: Team Pairing
stem:
A manager must pair four new hires (Priya, Quinn, Ravi, Sam) with four mentors (Wren, Xia, Yousef, Zane) for a six-month programme. Each mentor takes exactly one new hire. Wren mentors Sam. Xia will only mentor Ravi. Yousef refuses to mentor Quinn.

Which of the following pairings of new hires with mentors is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Wren mentors Sam and Xia mentors Ravi. That leaves Yousef and Zane to pair with Priya and Quinn. Yousef refuses Quinn, so Yousef = Priya and Zane = Quinn. Final pairing: Priya-Yousef, Quinn-Zane, Ravi-Xia, Sam-Wren — option A. Option B swaps Yousef and Zane, breaking the Yousef/Quinn constraint. Option C places Priya with Xia (only Ravi allowed). Option D puts Quinn with Wren and Sam with Zane, breaking Wren=Sam.

title: Cycle Helmet Law
stem: Should it be made compulsory for all adult cyclists to wear helmets to reduce head injuries on UK roads?
answer_reason: A directly links the action (mandatory helmets) to the outcome (reduced head injuries) with specific evidence. B addresses practicality but not head injuries. C is opinion-based and narrow. D addresses a tangential outcome (physical activity) rather than head injuries. A is the strongest.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a 2022 review of UK hospital data found cyclists wearing helmets had 45% fewer serious head injuries than those without, so a legal requirement would directly reduce head injuries.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; helmets are inexpensive and most cyclists already carry one.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; some cyclists find helmets uncomfortable on long rides.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; mandatory helmet laws discourage some people from cycling, which reduces physical activity across the population.

title: Lab Access
stem: A key card cannot unlock the laboratory unless it has been registered this month. Every key card registered this month shows a green indicator light. Only senior staff may register more than one key card. No visitor is senior staff.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every key card that can unlock the laboratory shows a green indicator light.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: A card can only unlock the lab if it has been registered this month, and every registered card shows a green indicator. So any unlocking card must show green.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a key card shows a green indicator light, it must have been registered this month.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premise is one-way: registered → green. Other cards could also display green for unrelated reasons, so green does not guarantee registration.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No visitor may register more than one key card.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only senior staff may register more than one card, and no visitor is senior staff, so no visitor has that privilege.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every visitor has been issued a key card that unlocks the laboratory.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premises say nothing about whether visitors are issued unlocking cards. Unmentioned = No.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a key card has not been registered this month, it cannot unlock the laboratory.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: This is the contrapositive of the "unless" rule: unlocking requires registration, so failing to register means the card cannot unlock the lab.

title: Remote Working Study
stem: A management consultancy reports that teams who adopted fully remote working in 2023 saw a 12% rise in self-reported productivity. Critics note the same teams also reported higher rates of burnout and that the productivity measure relied on self-assessment rather than objective output metrics. The consultancy acknowledges these limitations but argues the results still support remote working.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Remote working caused a 12% rise in productivity for the teams studied.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage reports a rise coinciding with remote working — not a proven causal link. Correlation is not causation.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The productivity measure in the study was based on self-assessment.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage explicitly states the productivity measure relied on self-assessment rather than objective output metrics.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The teams studied reported higher burnout after adopting remote working.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Directly stated by the critics cited in the passage.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The consultancy considers remote working unsuitable for all teams.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The consultancy still argues the results support remote working, not that it is unsuitable for all teams.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Objective productivity data would show the same 12% rise.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: No objective data is reported; the passage says the measure was self-assessment. We cannot predict what objective data would show.

title: UK Export Orders
stem:
A manufacturer ships 100 orders. 45 are exported, 40 are bulk orders, 55 are dispatched from within the UK region.

Among exported orders, 20 are also bulk. Among bulk orders, 25 are dispatched from within the UK region. Among exported orders, 22 are dispatched from within the UK region. 12 orders fall into all three categories. 18 orders are none of these three.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 12 orders are in all three categories and 18 are outside. Scan — A shows 15 in the centre — eliminate A. D shows 25 outside — eliminate D. That leaves B and C. The stem says 20 are exported and bulk, and 12 of those are also inside UK, so exported-and-bulk only = 20 − 12 = 8. B shows 8 ✓. C shows 10 — eliminate C. Answer: B.

title: Independent Alarms
stem:
A warehouse has two independent smoke alarms. Alarm X correctly triggers in 90% of fires. Alarm Y correctly triggers in 80% of fires.

What is the probability that at least one alarm triggers in the event of a fire?
answer_reason: P(neither triggers) = P(X fails) × P(Y fails) = 0.10 × 0.20 = 0.02. P(at least one triggers) = 1 − 0.02 = 0.98 = 98%.

title: Sterile Kits
stem: A surgical kit is safe to use if and only if it has been sterilised and sealed. All sealed kits carry a blue tag. Sterilisation is necessary for a kit to be reused. Some kits without blue tags have been opened.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every safe-to-use kit carries a blue tag.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Safe to use requires sealing, and every sealed kit carries a blue tag — therefore every safe kit carries a blue tag.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: A kit without a blue tag cannot be reused.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Reuse requires sterilisation, not sealing. A kit could be sterilised but not sealed — so it might lack a blue tag yet still meet the reuse condition.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some opened kits have not been sealed.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some kits without blue tags have been opened. Every sealed kit has a blue tag, so a no-blue-tag kit is not sealed. These opened, no-tag kits are therefore unsealed.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a kit has been sterilised, it is safe to use.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Safe to use requires BOTH sterilisation AND sealing. Sterilisation alone is not enough.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every safe-to-use kit can be reused.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Sterilisation is a necessary condition for reuse, not a sufficient one. A safe kit meets the sterilisation requirement but may fail other reuse requirements the premises do not list.

title: Sugar Tax on Snacks
stem: Should the government extend the sugar tax from soft drinks to all packaged snack foods to reduce childhood obesity?
answer_reason: B links the action (tax on snacks) to the outcome (childhood obesity) with specific evidence and NHS modelling. A assumes transfer between categories without evidence. C addresses tax revenue, not obesity. D makes a sweeping assumption that contradicts established evidence and ignores diet as a factor.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; households with young children already buy fewer sugary soft drinks since the 2018 tax, so extending it will make them buy fewer snacks too.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; data from the UK soft drink levy shows a 10% reduction in sugar consumption among children since 2018, and NHS modelling predicts a similar tax on snacks would cut childhood obesity rates by 5–7% over ten years.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; food manufacturers would simply reformulate products to avoid the tax, so the tax would collect little revenue.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; childhood obesity is caused by low physical activity, not by diet.

title: Import Warehouse
stem:
A warehouse receives 120 consignments in a month. 55 are imported, 48 are perishable, and 40 require cold storage. 18 are imported and perishable, 14 are imported and requiring cold storage, and 22 are perishable and requiring cold storage. 8 fall into all three categories. 35 do not fall into any of these three categories.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Two freebies: 8 consignments are in all three categories and 35 fall outside all three. Scan — C shows 12 in the centre, stem says 8 — eliminate C. D shows 40 outside, stem says 35 — eliminate D. That leaves A and B. The stem says 18 are imported and perishable, 8 of those are also cold storage, so imported-and-perishable only = 18 − 8 = 10. A shows 10 ✓. B shows 14 — eliminate B. Answer: A.

title: Delivery Vehicles
stem: A courier company runs 80 vehicles. 50 are vans and the rest are motorbikes. Every motorbike is electric. None of the red vehicles are motorbikes. Half of the vans are white.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every red vehicle is a van.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The fleet is vans or motorbikes. No motorbike is red, so any red vehicle must be a van.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some motorbikes are red.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage says none of the red vehicles are motorbikes — so no motorbike is red.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All electric vehicles in the fleet are motorbikes.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Every motorbike is electric, but vans could also be electric — we have no information ruling that out.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: There are exactly 25 white vans in the fleet.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Half of the 50 vans are white, which is 25 vans.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: There are more white vehicles than red vehicles in the fleet.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: We know 25 vans are white, but we do not know the number of red vehicles (only that none are motorbikes). The comparison cannot be made.

title: Regional Rainfall
stem: The table shows average monthly rainfall (mm) in four UK regions over four months in 2024.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Scotland had the highest rainfall in every month shown.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Scotland 110 > NW 92, SE 52, Mid 65 in April; Scotland 95 > others in May; Scotland 84 > others in June; Scotland 70 > others in July.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Rainfall fell in every region between April and July.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: NW 92→58, SE 52→38, Mid 65→48, Scotland 110→70. Every region saw rainfall fall.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The South East had less than half the rainfall of Scotland in April.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Half of 110 is 55. The South East had 52, which is less than 55.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The Midlands typically has a drier climate than the South East.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The table shows the opposite — Midlands rainfall exceeds South East rainfall in every month shown. "Typically" also extrapolates beyond the four months of data.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The North West recorded exactly 292 mm of rainfall across the four months.

title: Bloons and Grems
stem: All bloons are grems. Some grems are sprocks. No sprocks are doofs. Most doofs are nims.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some bloons are sprocks.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Bloons are grems, and only some grems are sprocks. The bloons could all fall among the non-sprock grems, so we cannot guarantee any bloon is a sprock.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some grems are not doofs.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some grems are sprocks, and no sprocks are doofs. So those sprock-grems are not doofs — at least some grems are not doofs.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No bloons are doofs.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: We know nothing about whether bloons are doofs. Bloons are grems, but grems are not restricted from being doofs.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Most nims are doofs.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Reverse inference. "Most doofs are nims" does not mean most nims are doofs — the nim population could be much larger.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All bloons are grems.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Directly stated in the premises.

title: Booking Order
stem:
Five consecutive appointments on Monday morning were booked by Aisha, Ben, Chloe, Dan, and Ellie (not necessarily in that order). Dan was booked immediately before Ellie. Aisha was booked before Ben, with at least one other person between them. Chloe was not the first or last appointment. Ben was not the last appointment.

Which of the following lists the appointments in order, from first to last, in a way that is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Dan is immediately before Ellie, so Dan-Ellie occupy consecutive positions. Ben is not last, so Ellie must be last — placing Dan-Ellie at positions 4-5. That leaves positions 1, 2, 3 for Aisha, Ben, Chloe. Chloe cannot be first or last, so Chloe is in position 2. Aisha is before Ben with at least one person between them, so Aisha = 1 and Ben = 3 (with Chloe between them). Order: Aisha, Chloe, Ben, Dan, Ellie — option A.

title: Plastic Cutlery Ban
stem: Should single-use plastic cutlery be banned nationwide to reduce marine plastic pollution?
answer_reason: A connects the action (ban) to the outcome (marine pollution) with evidence that cutlery is a significant source. B addresses preference, not pollution. C addresses business cost, not pollution. D deflects by comparing sources but does not address whether banning cutlery would still reduce pollution.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a recent beach survey found plastic cutlery in the top five items recovered from UK coastlines, and a national ban would remove this source of marine litter.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; plastic cutlery is unpleasant to use compared with wooden alternatives.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; many small takeaways rely on plastic cutlery and would find replacements expensive.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; most marine plastic pollution comes from fishing gear, not cutlery.

title: Workforce Profile
stem:
The diagram categorises a company's workforce by employment attributes. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a part-time remote worker who is neither a graduate trainee nor a contractor?
answer_reason: The question asks for a person inside workforce, remote worker, and part-time, but outside graduate trainee and contractor. Letter P is only in the workforce, no attribute. Letter Q is in the workforce and remote worker but not part-time. Letter R is in the workforce, remote worker, and graduate trainee — includes graduate trainee, which is excluded. Letter S is in the workforce, remote worker, and part-time, and outside graduate trainee and contractor — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter S.

title: Staff Benefits Portal
stem:
The diagram shows how company staff are registered for the staff benefits portal. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a staff member who is registered on the portal and takes up the travel pass benefit but no other benefit?
answer_reason: The question asks for staff inside registered AND travel pass, and outside every other benefit. Letter P is registered only, no benefit. Letter Q is registered and cycle-to-work, not travel pass. Letter R is registered and on the dental plan, not travel pass. Letter U is inside registered and travel pass, and outside every other benefit — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter U.

title: Night Delivery Rules
stem: No parcel may be delivered at night unless the recipient has opted in to night deliveries. All platinum members have opted in to night deliveries. Some gold members have opted in to night deliveries. No trial account has opted in to night deliveries.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a parcel is delivered at night, the recipient has opted in to night deliveries.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The "unless" rule makes opt-in a necessary condition for night delivery. Any night-delivered parcel goes to an opted-in recipient.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every gold member receives parcels at night.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only some gold members have opted in, not all. Even those who have opted in are not guaranteed to receive night deliveries — opt-in is necessary, not sufficient.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No trial account receives parcels at night.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Trial accounts have not opted in, and night delivery requires opt-in, so no trial account can receive a night delivery.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Everyone who has opted in to night deliveries is a platinum member.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Reverse inference. Some gold members have also opted in, so opt-in does not imply platinum status.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All platinum members receive parcels at night.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Platinum members have opted in, but opt-in is a necessary condition for night delivery, not a sufficient one. We cannot conclude every platinum member is delivered to at night.

title: Engineer Certification
stem: Only chartered engineers may sign off on a structural design. Every chartered engineer has passed the professional review. Some graduates have passed the professional review. No apprentice has passed the professional review.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Anyone who signs off on a structural design has passed the professional review.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only chartered engineers may sign off, and every chartered engineer has passed the review — so anyone signing off has passed.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No apprentice may sign off on a structural design.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Signing off requires being a chartered engineer, and that requires passing the review. Apprentices have not passed, so they are not chartered and cannot sign off.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every graduate is a chartered engineer.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some graduates have passed the review, but the premises do not say passing makes someone chartered. We cannot conclude any graduate is chartered.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some graduates may sign off on a structural design.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Signing off requires being a chartered engineer. The premises never confirm that for any graduate.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every chartered engineer may sign off on a structural design.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: "Only chartered engineers may sign off" — this places the permission with chartered engineers as a class.

title: Plonks and Quilks
stem: All plonks are quilks. Some quilks are not rambos. Every rambo is a skerrit. Most skerrits are not plonks.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some quilks are skerrits.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Every rambo is a skerrit, but the premises never confirm any rambo is also a quilk. We cannot prove any overlap between quilks and skerrits.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All plonks are quilks.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Directly stated in the premises.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some plonks are not rambos.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: "Some quilks are not rambos" does not guarantee any of those non-rambo quilks are plonks. The plonks might all fall among the quilks that are rambos.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some skerrits are not plonks.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: "Most skerrits are not plonks" means more than 50% — which guarantees at least some skerrits are not plonks.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No rambo is a plonk.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Nothing in the premises excludes overlap between rambos and plonks. A rambo could also be a plonk.

title: Courier Bonuses
stem: A courier earns a performance bonus if and only if they deliver more than 40 parcels in a day. Every courier on the north route delivered more than 40 parcels yesterday. No trainee courier earned a performance bonus yesterday. Some couriers earned a performance bonus without being on the north route.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every courier on the north route earned a performance bonus yesterday.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: North route couriers all delivered more than 40 parcels, and the biconditional rule converts that directly into earning a bonus.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No trainee courier worked on the north route yesterday.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Every north route courier earned a bonus, but no trainee earned a bonus — so no trainee was on the north route.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every courier who earned a bonus delivered more than 40 parcels.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The biconditional "if and only if" runs both ways: earning a bonus implies delivering more than 40 parcels.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every courier who delivered more than 40 parcels was on the north route.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some bonus-earners are not on the north route. Those couriers still crossed the threshold, so there are off-route couriers who delivered more than 40 parcels.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Most couriers on the north route are trainees.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: No north route courier is a trainee (every north route courier earned a bonus; no trainee did). So zero, not "most," of the north route couriers are trainees.

title: Archive Entry
stem: A member may enter the archive room if and only if they have both a research pass and a security escort. All doctoral students have a research pass. A security escort is necessary to borrow any sealed manuscript. Some visitors have a security escort but no research pass.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every doctoral student may enter the archive room.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Doctoral students have a research pass, but archive entry also requires a security escort. The pass alone is not enough.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: A visitor without a research pass cannot enter the archive room.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Archive entry requires both a research pass and a security escort. Without the pass, the condition fails, so entry is impossible.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every visitor with a security escort has borrowed a sealed manuscript.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: A security escort is necessary to borrow a sealed manuscript, not sufficient. Having an escort does not mean the visitor has used it to borrow anything.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some visitors cannot enter the archive room.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some visitors have an escort but no research pass. Entry requires both, so these visitors cannot enter.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every person who has borrowed a sealed manuscript has a research pass.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Borrowing a sealed manuscript requires a security escort, but the premises say nothing about requiring a research pass for borrowing. Unmentioned — so cannot be concluded.

title: Energy Drinks Study
stem: A 2024 study reported that university students who consumed at least one energy drink a day scored 8% higher on short memory tests than students who consumed none. Critics of the study point out that the sample was self-selecting, as participants volunteered through an energy drink company's website. The study's authors note that they have not yet tested for long-term effects and do not claim that energy drinks cause the memory improvement.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Energy drinks cause an 8% improvement in short memory test scores among university students.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The authors themselves state they are not claiming causation. The 8% is a correlation observed in a self-selecting sample.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The participants in the study volunteered through an energy drink company's website.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Directly stated in the passage.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The study measured long-term effects of energy drink consumption.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The authors explicitly state they have not yet tested for long-term effects.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Students who consumed at least one energy drink daily scored higher on the short memory tests in this study than students who consumed none.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The study reports an 8% higher score for the daily-consumption group — a directly stated comparison.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: A more representative sample would show the same 8% difference.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Critics flag the self-selecting sample as a potential problem. We cannot predict what a different sample would find.

title: Regional Sales Quarterly
stem: The table shows quarterly sales (in thousands of pounds) for four regional branches of a retailer in 2024.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Leeds recorded the highest sales in every quarter shown.
Bristol's sales grew every quarter compared with the previous quarter.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Bristol went 150 → 160 → 155 between Q2 and Q3, so sales fell in Q3.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Cardiff's Q4 sales were more than 30% higher than its Q1 sales.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Cardiff went 120 → 160, a rise of 40. 40 ÷ 120 ≈ 33.3%, which is more than 30%.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Belfast's total sales across the four quarters exceeded £400,000.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: 90 + 95 + 100 + 115 = 400. Values are in thousands, so the total is exactly £400,000 — not more.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Cardiff will overtake Bristol in total annual sales in 2025.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The table covers 2024 only. Projecting 2025 is extrapolation beyond the data.

title: Pet Adoption Centre
stem: A pet centre has 60 animals, of which 40 are cats and the rest are dogs. All of the dogs have been microchipped. None of the vaccinated animals are black. Half of the cats are vaccinated.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some cats are microchipped.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage only says all dogs are microchipped. It gives no information about cats being microchipped. We cannot conclude any cat is microchipped.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No vaccinated cat is black.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: No vaccinated animal is black. Cats are animals, so no vaccinated cat is black.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Exactly 20 cats at the centre are vaccinated.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Half of the 40 cats are vaccinated, which is 20 cats.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All of the dogs are vaccinated.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage says dogs are microchipped, not vaccinated. We have no information on dog vaccination.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every black animal at the centre is a cat.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All vaccinated animals are non-black, but the passage does not forbid unvaccinated dogs from being black. So a dog could be black.

title: Emergency Department Waits
stem: The table shows the median wait time (in minutes) for patients arriving at the emergency departments of three hospitals, split by triage category, in one week of March 2024.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Westbrook had the shortest median wait time in every triage category shown.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Immediate 2 < 3, 4. Urgent 24 < 28, 35. Standard 80 < 95, 110. Non-urgent 155 < 180, 210. Westbrook is lowest in every column.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: St Bede's median non-urgent wait was more than twice its median urgent wait.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Urgent = 35 minutes, so double is 70. Non-urgent = 210, which is six times the urgent wait — far more than double.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Westbrook treats a higher proportion of non-urgent patients than the other hospitals.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The table shows median wait times, not patient volumes or proportions. We cannot infer patient mix from wait times.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every hospital's median immediate wait was under 5 minutes in the week shown.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Royal Oak 3, St Bede's 4, Westbrook 2 — all under 5 minutes.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Immediate patients at all three hospitals will wait under 5 minutes in 2025.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The table covers one week in March 2024. We cannot extrapolate to 2025.

title: Four-Day Week Trial
stem: A technology consultancy claims that software teams who adopted a four-day work week in 2023 reported a 15% increase in code output per hour. Critics note the teams that opted into the trial were pre-selected as high performers and that output was measured by lines of code rather than a standardised task metric. The consultancy acknowledges the sampling issue but maintains that the trial supports rolling out four-day weeks across the sector.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Adopting a four-day work week causes software teams to produce 15% more code per hour.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage describes a reported increase for one self-selected group. Causation is not established, and critics highlight confounding factors.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The teams in the trial were selected based on their existing performance levels.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Critics note the teams were pre-selected as high performers — directly stated.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Output in the trial was measured using a standardised task metric.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage says output was measured by lines of code, not a standardised task metric.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The consultancy recommends rolling out four-day weeks across the sector.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The consultancy maintains the trial supports a sector-wide roll-out — that is a recommendation.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If an average-performing team adopted a four-day week, their code output would rise by 15%.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The trial measured only pre-selected high performers. Extrapolating to average teams is unsupported.

title: Relay Race Order
stem:
Five runners — Anita, Blake, Cora, Diya, and Eli — finish a relay race in some order from first to fifth. Blake finishes immediately after Anita. Cora finishes before both Anita and Diya. Eli does not finish first. Diya is not last.

Which of the following lists the runners in order from first to last, consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Cora must be before Anita and Diya, so Cora is in position 1 or 2. Blake is immediately after Anita, so Anita+Blake are consecutive. Diya is not last and Eli is not first. Testing Cora = 1: remaining positions 2-5 for Anita, Blake, Diya, Eli. Anita-Blake must be consecutive, Diya ≠ position 5, Eli ≠ position 1 (already satisfied). Anita=2, Blake=3, Diya=4, Eli=5 works — all constraints satisfied. Option C.

title: Sibling Ages
stem:
The mean age of four siblings is 15 years. Bea is twice Cal's age. Dev is four years older than Cal. Eli is two years older than Bea.

How old is Cal?
answer_reason: Total of all four ages = 4 × 15 = 60. Let Cal = C. Bea = 2C, Dev = C + 4, Eli = 2C + 2. Sum: C + 2C + (C + 4) + (2C + 2) = 6C + 6 = 60, so 6C = 54 and C = 9.

title: Volunteer Matching
stem:
Four volunteers — Priya, Quinn, Ravi, and Sam — each join a different one of four charities: Hope, Listen, Move, and Shelter. Ravi joins Move. Priya does not join Listen. Quinn joins Hope. Sam does not join Shelter.

Which of the following pairings of volunteers with charities is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Ravi = Move and Quinn = Hope are fixed. That leaves Priya and Sam to pair with Listen and Shelter. Priya ≠ Listen, so Priya = Shelter and Sam = Listen. Final: Priya-Shelter, Quinn-Hope, Ravi-Move, Sam-Listen — option A.

title: Quiz Team Selection
stem:
A firm picks an 8-member inter-department quiz team. Each of four departments contributes exactly 2 members, split evenly between one junior and one senior. A fair draw resolves any department with more nominations than slots. The nominations are shown in the table below.

Which of the following lists the volunteers who take part in the fair draw?
answer_reason: Each department must produce 1 junior and 1 senior. Marketing, IT, and HR each have exactly 1 junior and 1 senior — no draw needed. Finance has 1 junior (Dev, exact) and 2 seniors (Ella, Fran) for 1 senior slot — Ella and Fran go to the fair draw. Option B.

title: Street House Numbers
stem:
Four houses sit in a row on one side of a street, numbered 1, 3, 5, and 7 from left to right. The Aran, Bruno, Chen, and Dumas families each live in one of these houses, one family per house. The Bruno family lives at a lower number than the Aran family. The Chen family does not live at an end house. The Dumas family lives at number 7. The Aran family does not live next to the Dumas family.

Which family lives at number 1?
answer_reason: Dumas = 7 (given). Aran is not next to Dumas, so Aran ≠ 5, meaning Aran is at 1 or 3. Bruno's number must be lower than Aran's, so Aran cannot be at 1 — that leaves Aran = 3 and Bruno = 1. Chen is not at an end, so Chen = 5 (the only remaining middle number). Bruno at number 1.

title: Mandatory First Aid Training
stem: Should workplace first aid training be made mandatory for all UK employees to reduce the severity of workplace injuries?
answer_reason: B links the action (mandatory training) to the outcome (reduced injury severity) with specific HSE evidence. A addresses employee confidence, not injury severity. C focuses on a narrow subgroup ("some industries") rather than the broad population. D addresses productivity, not injury severity.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; many employees report feeling more confident at work after completing first aid training.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a 2023 HSE analysis of UK workplaces found that sites with trained first aiders saw 30% fewer injuries escalate to hospital admission, directly reducing injury severity.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; some industries rarely see serious workplace injuries, making the training redundant for those workers.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; mandatory training would take time away from productive work tasks for every employee.

title: E-Scooter Pavement Ban
stem: Should e-scooters be banned from city centre pavements to improve pedestrian safety?
answer_reason: A links the action (pavement ban) to the outcome (pedestrian safety) with transport authority evidence. B is opinion-based and does not address safety. C addresses rider welfare, not pedestrian safety. D deflects by comparing sources but does not address whether the ban would still help.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; transport authority data from five UK cities showed pedestrian injuries fell by 42% after pavement e-scooter bans, directly improving pedestrian safety.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; many pedestrians report feeling uncomfortable sharing pavements with e-scooters.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; e-scooter riders need somewhere safe to travel, and pavements are often the safest option.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; pavement cyclists cause similar safety problems, so banning only e-scooters would not fix the wider issue.

title: Later Sunday Openings
stem: Should UK retail chains delay Sunday trading hours to start at 11am instead of earlier, to improve the wellbeing of retail staff?
answer_reason: B connects the action (11am Sunday starts) to the outcome (staff wellbeing) with workforce health data. A addresses shopper preference, not wellbeing. C focuses on "some" staff — a narrow group, not the full workforce. D addresses revenue, not wellbeing.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; many shoppers prefer to shop later on Sundays anyway.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a 2022 review of UK retail workforce health found an 11am Sunday start improved reported sleep quality by 18% and reduced staff sick days by 9%, directly improving staff wellbeing.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; some retail staff prefer starting early on Sundays so that they can finish earlier.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; retail chains would lose revenue from customers who shop before 11am.

title: Prescription Charges for Over-60s
stem: Should NHS prescription charges be abolished for all adults over the age of 60 to improve long-term health outcomes in this age group?
answer_reason: B links the action (abolishing charges for over-60s) to the outcome (improved long-term health) with comparative health-economics evidence. A is anecdotal and does not address outcomes. C is a comparative deflection that never evaluates whether the proposed action would still help. D addresses NHS funding, not health outcomes for the over-60 group.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; pharmacists report that older patients frequently ask for cheaper alternatives to prescribed medicines.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a 2024 health-economics study found that in OECD countries where prescription charges were abolished for over-60s, hospital admissions in that age group fell by 12%, directly improving long-term health outcomes.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; adults over 60 are not the age group with the poorest long-term health outcomes in the UK.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; abolishing charges would reduce NHS funding available for other essential services.

title: Charity Shop Donations
stem:
A charity shop logs 90 donations in a month across three categories: clothes, books, and toys.

40 donations are clothes, 35 are books, and 28 are toys. 12 donations are both clothes and books, 10 donations are both clothes and toys, and 8 donations are both books and toys. 5 donations fall into all three categories. 12 donations fit none of the three categories.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 5 donations are in all three categories and 12 are outside. Scan — B shows 8 in the centre, stem says 5 — eliminate B. C shows 16 outside, stem says 12 — eliminate C. That leaves A and D. The stem says 12 are clothes and books, 5 of those also toys, so clothes-and-books only = 12 − 5 = 7. A shows 7 ✓. D shows 9 — eliminate D. Answer: A.

title: Bottle Production Stages
stem:
A factory logs 120 bottles produced in a shift across three sequential stages: filled, capped, and labelled. A bottle at a later stage has also passed every earlier stage.

20 bottles were filled but not capped. 30 bottles were filled and capped but not labelled. 60 bottles reached all three stages. 10 bottles did not enter production.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 10 bottles did not enter production and 60 bottles reached all three stages. Scan — B shows 22 filled-only, stem says 20 — eliminate B. C shows 65 at the all-three region, stem says 60 — eliminate C. D shows 15 outside, stem says 10 — eliminate D. A matches every stated value. Answer: A.

title: Wedding Roles
stem:
The diagram shows 120 people attending a wedding categorised by four roles: guest, helper, coordinator, and photographer. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a helper who is also a coordinator, but who is neither a guest nor a photographer?
answer_reason: The question asks for the region inside helper and coordinator but outside guest and photographer. Letter P sits inside guest only. Letter Q sits inside guest and helper — includes guest, which is excluded. Letter S sits inside coordinator and photographer — includes photographer, which is excluded. Letter R sits inside helper and coordinator, outside guest and photographer — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter R.

title: Library Workshop Attendance
stem:
A library runs two independent clubs and every member is in exactly one club. The Reading Club offers two workshops — Fiction and Poetry — and some members attend both. The Craft Club offers two workshops — Drawing and Bookbinding — and some members attend both. The diagram shows 120 members categorised by the workshops they attend. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a member who attends both Fiction and Poetry workshops, but is not in the Craft Club?
answer_reason: The two clubs are disjoint, so any Reading Club workshop region is automatically outside both Craft Club workshops. The question asks for the region inside both Fiction and Poetry. Letter P is Fiction only. Letter Q is Poetry only. Letter U is Drawing and Bookbinding — outside the Reading Club entirely. Letter R sits inside Fiction and Poetry, outside Drawing and Bookbinding — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter R.

title: Training Module Enrolments
stem:
A company offers four staff training modules arranged as a skills cycle: Leadership → Negotiation → Strategy → Communication → Leadership. Enrolments overlap only between modules that are adjacent in this cycle — no employee is enrolled in exactly a non-adjacent pair. The diagram shows 240 employees. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents an employee enrolled in both Negotiation and Strategy, and in no other module?
answer_reason: Overlaps exist only between adjacent modules in the cycle Leadership → Negotiation → Strategy → Communication → Leadership. The question asks for the region inside Negotiation and Strategy, and outside both Leadership and Communication. Letter T is Leadership and Negotiation. Letter V is Strategy and Communication. Letter W is Communication and Leadership. Letter U sits inside Negotiation and Strategy, outside Leadership and Communication — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter U.

title: Fruit Market Stock
stem:
A market logs 80 fruit items across three categories: imported, organic, and in season.

35 items are imported. 25 items are organic. 30 items are in season. 10 items are both imported and organic. 12 items are both imported and in season. No organic items are in season. 12 items fall into none of the three categories.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 10 imported and organic, 12 imported and in season, 12 outside. Scan — B shows 15 outside, stem says 12 — eliminate B. D shows 8 imported and organic, stem says 10 — eliminate D. That leaves A and C. The stem says no organic items are in season, so there should be no organic-and-in-season region. C shows 2 in that region — eliminate C. A matches every stated value. Answer: A.

title: Two Traffic Lights
stem:
A commuter passes through two traffic lights on the way to work. The lights operate independently. The first light is green 60% of the time. The second light is green 50% of the time.

What is the probability that both lights are green at the moment the commuter arrives?
answer_reason: Independent events, so P(both green) = P(first green) × P(second green) = 0.60 × 0.50 = 0.30 = 30%.

title: Dice Roll Game
stem:
A game costs £2 to play. A fair six-sided die is rolled. If the player rolls a 6, they win £10. If they roll any other number, they win nothing.

What is the expected value (winnings minus cost) of a single play?
answer_reason: Expected winnings = (1/6) × £10 + (5/6) × £0 ≈ £1.67. Expected value = expected winnings − cost = £1.67 − £2.00 ≈ −£0.33.

title: Sum on Two Dice
stem:
Two fair six-sided dice are rolled and the two top faces are added together.

What is the probability that the sum equals exactly 7?
answer_reason: There are 36 equally likely outcomes. The pairs summing to 7 are (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) — 6 outcomes. Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

title: Sixth-Form Subjects
stem:
A school has 80 sixth-formers. 45 study Maths, 30 study Physics, and 20 study both Maths and Physics. A sixth-former is picked at random from those studying Maths.

What is the probability that the chosen student also studies Physics?
answer_reason: Conditional probability: the denominator is the Maths group (45), not the whole year (80). Students who study both = 20. P(Physics | Maths) = 20 / 45 = 4/9.

title: Three-Day Rain Forecast
stem:
A weather forecaster states that the probability of rain on each of three consecutive days is independently 0.4.

What is the probability that it rains on at least one of the three days?
answer_reason: P(no rain on a single day) = 1 − 0.4 = 0.6. P(no rain on all three days) = 0.6 × 0.6 × 0.6 = 0.216. P(at least one day of rain) = 1 − 0.216 = 0.784 = 78.4%.

title: Westgate Library Loans
stem: Only members of Westgate Library may borrow reference books. A member who has borrowed a reference book cannot borrow another reference book unless the first has been returned. Every reference book has a yellow spine sticker. All reference books are shelved on the second floor.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Anyone who has borrowed a reference book must be a member of Westgate Library.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only members may borrow reference books, so every borrower is a member.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every book with a yellow spine sticker is a reference book.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premise says all reference books have yellow stickers, not the reverse. Other books could also have yellow stickers.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: A member currently holding one unreturned reference book may borrow a second reference book.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Directly contradicted — the premise says they cannot borrow another unless the first has been returned.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every book shelved on the second floor of Westgate Library is a reference book.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premise says all reference books are on the second floor, not that only reference books are there. Other books could also be shelved there.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: For a member to borrow a second reference book, they must first return the first one.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The "cannot … unless" premise makes returning the first book a necessary condition for borrowing the second.

title: Round-Robin Tennis Points
stem:
In a round-robin tennis tournament, five players each play every other player exactly once. A win awards 2 points to the winner and 0 to the loser; a drawn match awards 1 point to each player. At the end of the tournament, four of the players have scored 5 points each.

How many points did the fifth player score?
answer_reason: Five players playing every other player once gives 10 matches in total. Every match awards 2 points in total (either 2 + 0 or 1 + 1), so the tournament distributes 20 points. If four players have scored 5 each, that is 20 points accounted for — leaving 0 points for the fifth player.

title: Mandatory Cycle Helmets
stem: Should cycle helmets be made legally mandatory for all cyclists in the UK to reduce cycling-related head injuries?
answer_reason: A directly links the action (mandatory helmets) to the outcome (cycling head injuries) with peer-reviewed evidence and a concrete modelled reduction. B is emotional stereotyping and does not address head injury rates. C addresses comfort, not head injuries. D is a principle of personal freedom, not an argument about the outcome.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; peer-reviewed studies show helmet use reduces cycling-related head-injury risk by around 60%, and modelling based on UK cycling volumes suggests a mandatory law would prevent around 2,000 head injuries per year.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; many cyclists are reckless and need to be forced to protect themselves.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; helmets are uncomfortable and awkward to carry around when the cyclist is not on the bike.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; individuals should have the freedom to decide whether to wear a helmet.

title: Community Sports Participation
stem: The table shows the number of participants using five community sports centres in 2023 and 2024, and the percentage change year-on-year.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Total participants across the five centres were higher in 2024 than in 2023.
Sunbury had the highest number of participants in both years.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Sunbury was highest in 2023 (640) but in 2024 Parkview (598) overtook Sunbury (576).

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Lilyfield and Parkview both recorded an increase in participants.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Lilyfield rose from 420 to 462 and Parkview from 520 to 598 — both increases.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Riverdale will have the same number of participants in 2025 as in 2024.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Extrapolation — past stability does not guarantee future values.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every centre that recorded a decrease lost the same percentage of participants.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The only centres that decreased were Oakhurst (−10.0%) and Sunbury (−10.0%), which match.

title: Garden Centre Plants
stem:
A garden centre stocks 180 plant types. 60 are shade-tolerant, 75 are drought-tolerant, and 54 are frost-tolerant. 24 plant types are both shade-tolerant and drought-tolerant. 18 plant types are both drought-tolerant and frost-tolerant. No plant type is both shade-tolerant and frost-tolerant. 33 plant types are none of these three.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Two freebies: 33 plant types are outside all three categories, and the stem gives the two overlap counts directly — 24 shade-and-drought and 18 drought-and-frost. Scan — D shows 41 outside, not 33 — eliminate D. B shows 18 in the shade-and-drought overlap and 24 in the drought-and-frost overlap, the two numbers swapped — eliminate B. C shows 20 and 20 in those overlaps — eliminate C. A shows 24 and 18 in the overlaps and 33 outside. Answer: A.

title: Rare Nut Allergy Test
stem:
A rare nut allergy affects 1 in 500 people. A new skin-prick test correctly identifies 99% of true cases as positive (when the allergy is present) and correctly identifies 97% of non-cases as negative (when the allergy is absent). A randomly selected person tests positive.

Approximately what is the probability that this person actually has the allergy?
answer_reason: Imagine 100,000 people. About 200 have the allergy and 99,800 do not. True positives = 99% × 200 = 198. False positives = 3% × 99,800 = 2,994. Total positives ≈ 198 + 2,994 = 3,192. P(allergy | positive) ≈ 198 / 3,192 ≈ 6.2%. Option A (3%) matches the false-positive rate rather than the conditional probability. Option C (50%) is a naive assumption. Option D (99%) confuses the test's sensitivity with the chance of having the allergy.

title: Kitchen Assistant Screening
stem: Holding a Level 2 food hygiene certificate is necessary to work as a kitchen assistant at this restaurant. Passing the internal health screening is sufficient to be offered a shift. All kitchen assistants are required to wear a green apron. No one who has failed the internal health screening wears a green apron.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every kitchen assistant at this restaurant holds a Level 2 food hygiene certificate.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The certificate is stated as necessary for the job, so every kitchen assistant must hold one.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Anyone who passes the internal health screening must be a kitchen assistant.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Passing the screening is sufficient to be offered a shift, not sufficient to be a kitchen assistant specifically. They could be offered other roles.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every kitchen assistant at this restaurant has passed the internal health screening.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Kitchen assistants wear a green apron. No one who has failed the screening wears a green apron. By contrapositive, anyone wearing a green apron has passed the screening — so all kitchen assistants have passed.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Holding a Level 2 food hygiene certificate guarantees the holder a kitchen assistant job.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Necessary, not sufficient — the certificate is required, but having it doesn't guarantee the role.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Someone who has failed the internal health screening could still work as a kitchen assistant.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Kitchen assistants wear green aprons, and no one who has failed the screening wears a green apron — so a failed candidate cannot be a kitchen assistant.

title: Bench Seating Order
stem:
Six people — Anil, Beth, Carlos, Diya, Eun, and Faris — sit on a bench in a row numbered 1 to 6 (left to right). Anil is in position 4. Beth sits somewhere to Anil's right. Carlos sits directly next to Anil but not directly next to Beth. Faris sits at one of the two ends. Eun sits somewhere between Faris and Carlos. Diya sits to Beth's right.

Which of the following seating arrangements, listed from position 1 to position 6, is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Anil = 4 is fixed and Beth must be in 5 or 6. Carlos must be next to Anil; Carlos = 5 would put him next to Beth, so Carlos = 3. Faris at an end: Faris = 6 forces Eun = 5 and leaves no right-of-Anil seat for Beth, so Faris = 1. Eun sits between Faris (1) and Carlos (3), so Eun = 2. Diya is to Beth's right, so Beth = 5 and Diya = 6. Order: Faris, Eun, Carlos, Anil, Beth, Diya.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Carlos, Eun, Faris, Anil, Beth, Diya

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Faris, Eun, Carlos, Anil, Beth, Diya

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Faris, Eun, Carlos, Anil, Diya, Beth

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Faris, Carlos, Eun, Anil, Beth, Diya

title: Universal Free School Meals
stem: Should all UK primary school pupils receive free school meals regardless of family income, in order to improve their educational attainment?
answer_reason: A links the action (free universal meals) to the outcome (educational attainment) using a direct pilot study result. B addresses parental convenience, not attainment. C raises cost, which is about feasibility rather than attainment. D addresses preference, not attainment.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a four-year government pilot of universal free school meals recorded an 8% rise in pupils' average reading and maths scores compared to a matched control group.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; many parents find packing school lunches stressful in the mornings.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; schools already have enough costs to cover and cannot afford a universal meal programme.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; not every pupil wants to eat school-provided food rather than their own lunch.

title: Cubicle Productivity Survey
stem: A business research firm surveyed 500 office workers before and after their company moved them from an open-plan layout to private cubicles. After the move, 62% of respondents reported feeling more productive. Only 8% reported feeling less productive, and the remainder reported no change. The firm's report concludes that private cubicles cause improvements in productivity, though some commentators argue the change may reflect the novelty of the new layout and predict that perceived benefits will fade within a year.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: More than half of the surveyed workers reported feeling more productive after the move.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: 62% is more than half, and this is directly stated in the passage.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Perceived productivity gains from the cubicle layout will have disappeared within twelve months of the move.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: This is a commentator prediction, not proven by the passage. It is also an extrapolation beyond the data.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Measured productivity rose after the office layout was changed.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage reports workers' self-reported feelings of productivity, not measured productivity, and presents the causal claim as the firm's contested conclusion.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The survey recorded views from the same group of workers before and after the layout change.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states the firm surveyed the 500 workers before and after their company moved them — the same group measured twice.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Open-plan desks are less suitable for productivity than private cubicles.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage's causal claim is contested by commentators, so it cannot be treated as established fact.

title: Market Research Interests
stem:
A market research firm interviews 140 respondents and records four product interests. 42 are interested in podcasts, 30 in audiobooks, 36 in yoga apps, and 28 in running trackers. 14 respondents are interested in both podcasts and audiobooks. 12 respondents are interested in both yoga apps and running trackers. No respondent who is interested in podcasts or audiobooks is also interested in yoga apps or running trackers. 30 respondents are interested in none of these four categories.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Two freebies from the stem: 14 respondents are interested in both podcasts and audiobooks, and 12 are interested in both yoga apps and running trackers. Scan — B shows 12 in the podcast-and-audiobook overlap and 14 in the yoga-and-running overlap (the two numbers swapped) — eliminate B. C shows 18 and 16 in the two overlaps, neither matches — eliminate C. D shows 16 and 14 in the overlaps — eliminate D. A shows 14 and 12 in the two overlaps. Answer: A.

title: Two Packing Machines
stem:
A factory has two independent packing machines. Machine A produces a defective packet with probability 0.05. Machine B produces a defective packet with probability 0.08. A supervisor picks one packet at random from Machine A and one packet at random from Machine B.

What is the probability that at least one of the two packets is defective?
answer_reason: P(A not defective) = 0.95 and P(B not defective) = 0.92. Independence gives P(neither defective) = 0.95 × 0.92 = 0.874. So P(at least one defective) = 1 − 0.874 = 0.126. Option A (0.004) is P(both defective). Option C (0.130) is 0.05 + 0.08, which over-counts the case where both are defective. Option D (0.874) is P(neither defective).

title: Pharmacy Dispensing
stem: Only registered pharmacists may dispense prescription-only medicines at this pharmacy. All registered pharmacists have completed the continuing professional development (CPD) programme this year. Some assistants have also completed the CPD programme.
