No assistant has dispensed prescription-only medicines at this pharmacy.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Everyone who has dispensed prescription-only medicines at this pharmacy is a registered pharmacist.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: "Only registered pharmacists may dispense" — if someone dispensed, they must be a registered pharmacist.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every registered pharmacist has dispensed a prescription-only medicine at this pharmacy this year.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Pharmacists are permitted to dispense, but the premises don't state that each one actually has.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some people who have completed the CPD programme have not dispensed prescription-only medicines at this pharmacy.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some assistants have completed CPD, and no assistant has dispensed — so those CPD-completing assistants have not dispensed.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If someone has not completed the CPD programme this year, they cannot be a registered pharmacist.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Contrapositive of "all registered pharmacists have completed CPD".

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Everyone who has completed the CPD programme is a registered pharmacist.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Reverse inference — some assistants have also completed CPD, and assistants are not pharmacists here.

title: Dog Training Awards
stem:
Four dog trainers — Gemma, Harsh, Ira, and Jonas — each train a different breed (beagle, collie, spaniel, whippet) and competed in four events (sprint, agility, scent, retrieval). Each trainer won exactly one event. Gemma did not train the beagle. The collie's trainer won retrieval. Harsh trained the whippet and did not win scent. Ira won sprint but did not train the collie. Jonas trained the beagle.

Which trainer-breed-event combination is correct?
answer_reason: Jonas trained the beagle and Harsh trained the whippet, leaving collie and spaniel for Gemma and Ira. Ira did not train the collie, so Ira = spaniel and Gemma = collie. The collie's trainer won retrieval, so Gemma won retrieval. Ira won sprint (given). Harsh did not win scent, and sprint and retrieval are taken, so Harsh won agility. That leaves scent for Jonas. So Ira — spaniel — sprint, option C.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Gemma trained the spaniel and won retrieval.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Harsh trained the whippet and won scent.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Ira trained the spaniel and won sprint.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Jonas trained the beagle and won agility.

title: Opt-In Receipts
stem: Should large UK retailers be required to stop issuing paper receipts by default (offering them only on request) to reduce paper waste?
answer_reason: A links the action (opt-in receipts) to the outcome (paper waste reduction) with two concrete pieces of evidence. B addresses shopper preference, not paper waste. C addresses a narrow subgroup (older shoppers), not the overall waste outcome. D addresses returns convenience, not waste.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; UK retail paper receipts account for an estimated 53,000 tonnes of paper waste per year, and trials of a request-only approach in pilot retailers cut receipt paper use by over 80%.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; most shoppers already find paper receipts annoying and discard them immediately after leaving the shop.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; some older shoppers will struggle to keep track of purchases without a printed receipt.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; receipts are useful when customers want to return products to the shop.

title: Warehouse Box Colours
stem: A warehouse holds 90 boxes. Half of them are cardboard and the rest are wooden. Every wooden box is green. Two-thirds of the cardboard boxes are red, and the remaining cardboard boxes are blue. No red box contains fragile items.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every green box in the warehouse is a wooden box.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All cardboard boxes are either red or blue, so no cardboard box is green. Every green box must therefore be wooden.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every blue box in the warehouse is a cardboard box.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All wooden boxes are green, so no wooden box is blue. Any blue box must be cardboard.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: There are more green boxes than red boxes in the warehouse.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: 45 wooden boxes are all green. Red boxes are two-thirds of 45 cardboard boxes = 30. 45 > 30.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some cardboard boxes in the warehouse are green.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All cardboard boxes are red (two-thirds) or blue (the remainder) — none are green.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every box in the warehouse that contains fragile items is blue.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Red boxes are excluded from carrying fragile items, but the data does not say fragile items are restricted to blue boxes — wooden (green) boxes could also hold them.

title: Unlabelled Bakery Cakes
stem:
A bakery has 90 cakes. 30 are sponge, 25 are chocolate, and 20 are gluten-free. 10 cakes are both sponge and chocolate. 9 cakes are both sponge and gluten-free. 8 cakes are both chocolate and gluten-free. 6 cakes are in all three categories. 36 cakes are plain.

Which of the following diagrams is consistent with the data?
answer_reason: Two freebies: 6 cakes are in all three categories (the centre triple overlap) and 36 cakes are plain (outside). Scan — B shows 4 in the centre — eliminate B. C shows 42 outside — eliminate C. That leaves A and D. Each shape's regions must sum to its category total (sponge 30, chocolate 25, gluten-free 20). In D, the three shape totals come out as 29, 24, and 22 — none of them match the stated totals. In A, the three shapes sum to 30, 25, and 20 as required. Answer: A.

title: Exam Script Marking
stem: If an exam script is marked online, then the examiner recorded the result electronically. No script with a missing answer was marked online. Every script at centre 14 was marked online. Some scripts at centre 7 had missing answers.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If an examiner did not record a result electronically, that script was not marked online.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Contrapositive of "marked online → recorded electronically".

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No script at centre 14 had a missing answer.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Every script at centre 14 was marked online. No script with a missing answer was marked online. So no script at centre 14 had a missing answer.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every script at centre 7 had a missing answer.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premise says only "some" scripts at centre 7 had missing answers — under the UCAT reading of "some", this excludes "all".

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No script at centre 7 was marked online.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only some scripts at centre 7 had missing answers. The remaining centre 7 scripts could still have been marked online.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some scripts at centre 7 had their results recorded electronically.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premises only force electronic recording for online-marked scripts. We don't know whether any centre 7 script was actually marked online, so this is not guaranteed.

title: Who Broke the Vase
stem:
Four people at a shop — Ava, Ben, Cai, and Dee — are each suspected of breaking a vase. Exactly one of them broke it, and each makes one statement. Three of the statements are true and one is false.

Ava says: 'Ben broke it.'
Ben says: 'Dee broke it.'
Cai says: 'I did not break it.'
Dee says: 'Ben is lying.'

Who broke the vase?
answer_reason: Suppose Ben told the truth: then Dee broke it. Ava's claim "Ben broke it" is then false, and Dee's claim "Ben is lying" is also false — two false statements, breaking the one-liar rule. So Ben is the liar, and "Dee broke it" is false. The other three statements must all be true: Ava's "Ben broke it" is true, so Ben broke the vase. Cai's "I did not break it" and Dee's "Ben is lying" are consistent.

title: Loud Fireworks Ban
stem: Should the UK ban the retail sale of loud (above 80 dB) fireworks to the general public to reduce noise-related distress among pets and farm animals?
answer_reason: A links the action (ban on loud retail fireworks) to the outcome (animal distress) with evidence from similar bans abroad. B addresses human injuries, not animal distress. C observes that distress would not be fully eliminated, but reducing distress doesn't require eliminating every source. D addresses cultural importance, not the outcome.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a government-commissioned RSPCA report found that bans on loud retail fireworks in three comparable European countries reduced recorded pet distress incidents on fireworks nights by around 70%.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; fireworks are dangerous and many people injure themselves with them each year.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; large professional displays would still produce enough noise to cause animal distress.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; fireworks are an important part of British cultural celebrations.

title: City Air Quality
stem: The table shows the annual mean PM2.5 air pollution level (micrograms per cubic metre) for four UK cities over five years.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Portmire's PM2.5 level decreased every year from 2020 to 2024.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Portmire: 18.0 → 17.2 → 16.5 → 14.8 → 13.1. Each year is lower than the previous one.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: In 2024, Eastbrook had the lowest PM2.5 level of the four cities.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: 2024 values: Portmire 13.1, Ashford 14.5, Eastbrook 8.2, Thornhill 21.8. Eastbrook's 8.2 is the lowest.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Ashford's air quality improved from 2020 to 2024.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Ashford's PM2.5 rose from 12.5 to 14.5 — higher PM2.5 means worse air quality, not better.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Thornhill's PM2.5 will fall further in 2025.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Past readings cannot be extrapolated to a future year; the data does not forecast 2025.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Portmire's PM2.5 fell by more than 25% between 2020 and 2024.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Drop = 18.0 − 13.1 = 4.9. As a percentage of 2020: 4.9 ÷ 18.0 ≈ 27.2%, which is greater than 25%.

title: Artisan Food Production
stem:
The diagram shows 120 artisan food products categorised by five production-cycle tags: foraged, fermented, cured, smoked, and bottled. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a product that is both foraged and fermented, but is not cured, smoked, or bottled?
answer_reason: The question wants a product inside foraged and fermented but outside cured, smoked, and bottled. Letter P sits inside foraged only — fermented is missing. Letter V is inside fermented and cured — cured is excluded. Letter Y is inside foraged and bottled — bottled is excluded. Letter U is the region inside foraged and fermented but outside the other three stages.

title: Neighbourhood Burglar Alarm
stem:
In a neighbourhood, the probability that a given house is actually being burgled on any one night is 1 in 2,000. The alarm system fitted to every house triggers for 95% of active burglaries. When no burglary is in progress, it false-triggers on any given night with probability 3%.

If the alarm triggers at a randomly chosen house one night, approximately what is the probability that a burglary is actually in progress?
answer_reason: Imagine 200,000 houses. Active burglaries = 100, and 95% of alarms trigger → 95 genuine alarms. Non-burgled houses = 199,900, and 3% false-trigger → about 5,997 false alarms. Total alarms ≈ 95 + 5,997 = 6,092. P(burglary | alarm) ≈ 95 ÷ 6,092 ≈ 1.6%. The rare-event base rate drags the probability right down despite the 95% trigger rate.

title: Arc Welding Safety
stem: Workers cannot operate the arc welding machine without wearing a safety visor. Every welder at the Crewe plant is certified. No uncertified worker has operated the arc welding machine. Some apprentices at the Crewe plant are uncertified.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Any worker operating the arc welding machine is wearing a safety visor.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: "Cannot operate without" means operating requires the visor. Anyone operating must be wearing one.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every welder at the Crewe plant has operated the arc welding machine.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premises say they are certified, not that every welder has actually used this particular machine.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some apprentices at the Crewe plant have not operated the arc welding machine.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some apprentices are uncertified. No uncertified worker has operated the machine. So those uncertified apprentices have not operated it.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No apprentice at the Crewe plant is a welder.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some apprentices are uncertified, so they can't be welders — but other apprentices could be certified, and nothing rules out certified apprentices being welders.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Anyone wearing a safety visor at the Crewe plant must be operating the arc welding machine.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Reverse inference — the premises make the visor necessary for operating, not the other way round.

title: Round Table Seating
stem:
Five colleagues — Priya, Raj, Sam, Tina, and Uma — sit at a round table with chairs numbered 1 to 5 clockwise. Priya sits in chair 1 and Raj sits in chair 3. Sam does not sit in a chair directly next to Raj. Uma does not sit in chair 5.

Which chair does Sam occupy?
answer_reason: Chairs 1 (Priya) and 3 (Raj) are taken, leaving chairs 2, 4, and 5 for Sam, Tina, and Uma. The chairs directly next to Raj (chair 3) are 2 and 4, so Sam cannot be in either — Sam must be in chair 5. Uma's constraint only rules out chair 5 for Uma, which is consistent since Sam has taken it. Answer: chair 5.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Cannot be determined from the information given

title: Trainee Nurse Skills
stem:
The diagram shows 150 trainee nurses categorised by their completion of a core clinical module and four supplementary skill modules (venepuncture, cannulation, wound care, and triage). Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a trainee who has completed the core clinical module and the wound care module, but none of the other supplementary modules?
answer_reason: The question wants the core clinical module and wound care — but no other supplementary module. Letter P is core only, with no supplementary. Letter S is wound care only, with no core. Letter V is core and cannulation — wrong supplementary module. Letter W is the region where the core module overlaps wound care and no other supplementary module.

title: Festival Ticket Extras
stem: A festival has 180 ticket holders. A third of them hold a VIP pass and the rest hold standard passes. Every VIP pass includes drink tokens. Only some standard passes include drink tokens. Every ticket with parking also includes drink tokens. No standard pass without drink tokens includes parking.

decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Directly stated: every ticket with parking also includes drink tokens.

decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: VIP passes include drink tokens, but the stem says nothing about which passes include parking.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: A standard pass without drink tokens has no parking.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Directly stated — no standard pass without drink tokens includes parking.

title: Faculty Module Catalogue
stem:
The diagram shows 220 modules catalogued at a university, grouped by a Faculty tag and three department tags (Humanities, Sciences, Engineering). Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a module tagged to Faculty and to Humanities, but to no other department?
answer_reason: The question wants a module inside the Faculty tag and inside Humanities, but outside Sciences and Engineering. Letter P is inside the Faculty tag only, with no department. title: Two Hearts from a Deck
stem:
A standard 52-card deck contains 13 hearts. Two cards are drawn in sequence from the deck without replacement.

What is the probability that both cards are hearts?
answer_reason: P(first heart) = 13/52 = 1/4. After one heart is removed, 12 hearts remain in 51 cards, so P(second heart | first heart) = 12/51. P(both) = (13/52) × (12/51) = 156/2652 = 1/17. Option A (1/16) comes from treating the draws as if the card is replaced. Option C (1/26) is a wrong simplification. Option D (1/4) is just the first draw.

title: Library Book Tags
stem:
A library records 120 recently loaned books categorised by three tags. 54 are fiction, 40 are hardback, and 35 are bestsellers. 18 are both fiction and hardback. 14 are both fiction and bestseller. 12 are both hardback and bestseller. 8 books fall into all three categories. 27 books fall into none of these categories.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Two freebies: 8 books are in all three categories (the centre) and 27 books fall outside all three. Scan — B shows 6 in the centre, not 8 — eliminate B. C shows 31 outside, not 27 — eliminate C. That leaves A and D. The stem says 18 are both fiction and hardback; 8 of those are also bestsellers, so fiction-and-hardback only = 18 − 8 = 10. A shows 10 there ✓. D shows 6 there — eliminate D. Answer: A.

title: Fitness Studio Classes
stem:
The diagram shows 150 members of a fitness studio categorised by the classes they attend: yoga, pilates, and spin. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a member who attends yoga and spin but does not attend pilates?
answer_reason: The question wants a member inside yoga and spin but outside pilates. Letter S is yoga and pilates — missing spin and includes the wrong class. Letter U is pilates and spin — includes pilates, which is excluded. Letter V is all three classes — includes pilates. Letter T is the region inside yoga and spin but outside pilates.

title: Modern Language Enrolments
stem:
A sixth form has 80 students enrolled on modern language courses. 40 study French, 29 study German, and 28 study Spanish. 12 students study both French and German. 10 students study both German and Spanish. No student studies both French and Spanish. 5 students study none of these three languages.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Two freebies: 5 students study none of the three languages, and no student studies both French and Spanish — so the French and Spanish shapes must not overlap. Scan — C shows 7 outside, not 5 — eliminate C. The stem says 12 study French and German; B shows 10 in that overlap — eliminate B. D shows 14 there — eliminate D. A shows 12 in the French-and-German overlap, 10 in the German-and-Spanish overlap, no French-and-Spanish overlap, and 5 outside. Answer: A.

title: Company Pass Holders
stem:
The diagram shows 280 pass holders at a company categorised by three role tags: employee, manager, and director. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a pass holder tagged as a manager but not as a director?
answer_reason: The question wants a pass holder tagged as a manager but not as a director. Letter P is an employee only, no manager tag. Letter R is tagged as employee, manager, and director — includes the director tag, which is excluded. Letter S is outside every role tag. Letter Q is inside the manager region but outside the director region.

title: Art Class Levels
stem:
A school has 240 students registered across four art class levels. 80 attend beginner, 65 attend intermediate, 55 attend advanced, and 40 attend masterclass. 25 students attend both beginner and intermediate. 20 students attend both intermediate and advanced. 15 students attend both advanced and masterclass. 60 students do not attend any of these levels.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Two freebies: the stem gives 25 students attending beginner and intermediate, and 15 students attending advanced and masterclass. Scan — B shows 15 in the beginner-and-intermediate overlap and 25 in the advanced-and-masterclass overlap, the two numbers swapped — eliminate B. C shows 58 outside, not the stated 60 — eliminate C. That leaves A and D. The stem also gives 20 students attending intermediate and advanced. D shows 18 in that overlap — eliminate D. A matches every stated overlap and total. Answer: A.

title: Certified Sign-Off
stem: Only certified engineers may sign off on structural designs. All senior architects at this firm are certified engineers. Some project managers are senior architects. No graduate trainee is a certified engineer.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No graduate trainee may sign off on a structural design.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Signing off requires being a certified engineer; graduate trainees are not certified engineers.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every senior architect at this firm may sign off on structural designs.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Being a certified engineer is necessary for sign-off, but the stem never says it is sufficient. Senior architects meet the necessary condition only.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: At least one project manager is a certified engineer.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some project managers are senior architects, and every senior architect at this firm is a certified engineer, so at least one project manager is a certified engineer.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All project managers are senior architects.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only some project managers are senior architects. Extending to all is a quantifier shift.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Anyone permitted to sign off is a senior architect.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Sign-off requires being a certified engineer. Not all certified engineers are senior architects, so other certified engineers may also be allowed.

title: Zorbs and Flimbles
stem: All zorbs are flimbles unless they have been primed. No flimble is a druk. Some primed zorbs are druks. All druks are warbins.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No unprimed zorb is a druk.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Unprimed zorbs are flimbles (the 'unless' rule), and no flimble is a druk, so no unprimed zorb is a druk.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All zorbs are druks.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only some primed zorbs are druks. Unprimed zorbs cannot be druks because they are flimbles.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: At least one zorb is a warbin.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some primed zorbs are druks, and all druks are warbins, so at least one zorb is a warbin.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All warbins are druks.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The stem says all druks are warbins, not the reverse. Concluding all warbins are druks is a reverse-inference error.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some flimbles are druks.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The stem states 'no flimble is a druk'. This directly contradicts the statement.

title: Gluten-Free Aisle
stem: If a product is labelled 'gluten-free', it contains no wheat, barley, or rye. All products in aisle 4 are labelled 'gluten-free'. The oat biscuits in aisle 6 are not labelled 'gluten-free'. Some of the oat biscuits contain no wheat.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No product in aisle 4 contains wheat.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All aisle-4 products are labelled gluten-free, and gluten-free products contain no wheat.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The oat biscuits in aisle 6 contain wheat.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The stem says some oat biscuits contain no wheat. Not being labelled gluten-free does not imply containing wheat.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: A product that contains barley is not labelled 'gluten-free'.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Contrapositive of the rule: if gluten-free then no barley, so if barley then not gluten-free.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All products in aisle 6 are oat biscuits.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The stem names the oat biscuits in aisle 6 but does not state that aisle 6 contains only oat biscuits.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some oat biscuits are safe for people avoiding all gluten grains.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The stem only says some oat biscuits contain no wheat. Barley and rye content is unknown, so overall gluten safety cannot be concluded.

title: Sterile Instruments
stem: All surgical instruments are sterile unless they are in the pre-wash bin. No disposable instrument is placed in the pre-wash bin. Some instruments in the pre-wash bin are reusable. All reusable instruments need annual inspection.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All disposable instruments are sterile.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: No disposable instrument is in the pre-wash bin, so disposables fall under the 'all are sterile' rule.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No instrument in the pre-wash bin is sterile.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The 'unless' rule makes the pre-wash bin the exception to sterility: instruments in that bin are not sterile.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: At least one instrument in the pre-wash bin needs annual inspection.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some instruments in the bin are reusable, and all reusable instruments need annual inspection, so at least one bin instrument needs inspection.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All instruments that need annual inspection are reusable.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The stem says all reusables need inspection, not the reverse. Non-reusable instruments could also need inspection.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every reusable instrument is in the pre-wash bin.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only some instruments in the bin are reusable. Reusable instruments could also exist outside the bin.

title: Airport Monthly Passengers
stem: The table shows the number of passengers (in thousands) passing through four airport terminals over four months.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: August was the busiest month across the four terminals.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: August totals 560 + 495 + 275 + 200 = 1530 thousand. June = 1160, July = 1410, September = 1085. August is the highest.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: T4 will have more than 200 thousand passengers in October.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The table has no October data. Predicting future months is extrapolation beyond what is given.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: T1 had at least double the passenger count of T4 in every month shown.

title: Remote Work Wellness Study
stem: A recent study of office workers reported that those who worked from home at least two days a week had lower self-reported stress than those who came to the office every day. The authors proposed that the reduced commute time explained the difference. Critics noted that the remote-working group was older on average and more likely to have private home offices, both of which may independently reduce stress. The study did not measure productivity or long-term health.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Commuting less causes a reduction in self-reported stress.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The commute explanation is presented as the authors' proposal, not a proven causal link. Critics highlight possible confounders.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Remote workers in the study reported lower stress than daily office workers.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: This is directly stated in the passage.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Working from home improves long-term health.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The study did not measure long-term health, so this cannot be inferred.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The remote-working group in the study was on average older than the office-every-day group.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states this directly when describing the critics' concern.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Older workers are more likely to work from home.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage says this was true of the remote-working sample in this study; it does not claim it holds of older workers in general.

title: Mixed Fruit Basket
stem: A market basket contains 40 pieces of fruit. 24 are apples and the rest are pears. Three-quarters of the apples are green and the remainder are red. None of the red fruit are pears.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every pear in the basket is green.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The stem only tells us none of the red fruit are pears. Pears could be any non-red colour — green, yellow, or otherwise. 'Not red' does not mean 'green'.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The basket contains exactly six red apples.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: 24 apples total; three-quarters green = 18 green apples; the remainder = 24 − 18 = 6 red apples.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: There are more green apples than pears in the basket.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Green apples = 18; pears = 40 − 24 = 16. 18 > 16.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every red fruit in the basket is an apple.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: None of the red fruit are pears, and the only fruit types are apples and pears, so every red fruit must be an apple.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: There are more red fruit than pears.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Red fruit = 6 (red apples only, since no red pears). Pears = 16. 6 is not more than 16.

title: Quarterly Revenue Table
stem: The table shows quarterly revenue (in £ thousand) for four product lines at a manufacturer.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Alpha was the highest-revenue product line in Q4.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Q4 values: Alpha 165, Beta 72, Gamma 96, Delta 140. Alpha is highest.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Delta's revenue is stable because customer demand is unchanged.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The table shows stable revenue but gives no information about the cause.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Gamma's revenue grew by exactly 12 between each consecutive quarter.
Total revenue across all four lines grew from Q1 to Q4.
Beta will continue to decline into Q1 of the following year.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The table covers only four quarters. Projecting beyond them is extrapolation.

title: Relay Team Lineup
stem:
A relay team of six runners (Priya, Quinn, Ravi, Sam, Tomas, Uma) is ordered from first to sixth leg. Sam runs immediately before Ravi. Uma runs at some point after Tomas. Quinn runs the first leg. Priya runs the fifth leg. Tomas does not run the second leg.

Which of the following orders, from first to sixth leg, is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Quinn is fixed on leg 1 and Priya on leg 5. The Sam–Ravi block must be consecutive, so it sits on legs 2–3 or 3–4 (leg 4–5 would force Ravi into Priya's spot). Tomas cannot be on leg 2. Placing Sam–Ravi on legs 2–3 leaves Tomas and Uma for legs 4 and 6, with Uma after Tomas, so Tomas = 4 and Uma = 6. Order: Quinn, Sam, Ravi, Tomas, Priya, Uma — option C.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Quinn, Sam, Ravi, Uma, Priya, Tomas

decision_making_question_options.option_text: Quinn, Tomas, Sam, Ravi, Priya, Uma

title: Quiz Night Scores
stem:
Five friends played a quiz and their average score was 14. Alex scored two more than Blake. Cara scored five more than Blake. Dev scored one fewer than Blake. Ellis scored four more than Blake.

How many points did Blake score?
answer_reason: Total = 5 × 14 = 70. Let Blake = B. Alex = B + 2, Cara = B + 5, Dev = B − 1, Ellis = B + 4. Sum: B + (B + 2) + (B + 5) + (B − 1) + (B + 4) = 5B + 10 = 70. 5B = 60, so B = 12.

title: Project Assignment
stem:
Four employees (Mia, Noor, Omar, Paul) are each assigned to exactly one of four projects (Red, Blue, Green, Yellow). Each project has exactly one employee. Mia will not take Red. Noor takes either Red or Green. Omar takes Yellow if and only if Mia takes Blue. Paul does not take Green.

Which of the following assignments is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Mia is not on Red. Try Mia on Blue — then Omar must take Yellow (the biconditional). Noor takes Red or Green; Paul does not take Green, so Paul must take Red — but if Paul takes Red then Noor must take Green (the remaining option), satisfying the Noor constraint. Assignment: Mia Blue, Paul Red, Noor Green, Omar Yellow — option A. Option B puts Paul on Green. Option C puts Mia on Red. Option D puts Omar on Yellow without Mia on Blue, violating the biconditional.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Mia: Blue, Noor: Green, Omar: Yellow, Paul: Red

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Mia: Blue, Noor: Red, Omar: Yellow, Paul: Green

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Mia: Red, Noor: Green, Omar: Yellow, Paul: Blue

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Mia: Green, Noor: Red, Omar: Yellow, Paul: Blue

title: Shelf Arrangement
stem:
Five books (Atlas, Biology, Cooking, Dictionary, Encyclopedia) are arranged left to right on a shelf. The Dictionary is somewhere to the right of the Atlas. The Biology is immediately next to the Cooking. The Encyclopedia is at one of the ends. The Atlas is not at either end.

Which of the following arrangements, from left to right, is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: The Atlas must be in position 2, 3, or 4. The Encyclopedia must be at position 1 or 5. The Dictionary must be right of the Atlas, and Biology–Cooking must be adjacent. Option A has Atlas at position 1 — fails. Option B has the Dictionary to the left of the Atlas — fails. Option D has the Encyclopedia in the middle — fails. Option C places Encyclopedia at position 1, Atlas at 2, Biology at 3, Cooking at 4, Dictionary at 5; every constraint holds.

title: Ban Plastic Straws
stem: Should single-use plastic straws be banned in cafés to reduce marine plastic pollution?
answer_reason: B is the strongest: it addresses both the action (banning plastic straws in cafés) and the outcome (marine plastic pollution) with a specific, evidence-based figure on the café contribution. A addresses the action but ties it to a different outcome (customer opinion, not marine pollution). C is emotion-led and speaks to convenience rather than marine pollution. D is a comparative deflection — it may be true that other items contribute more, but it does not argue against the café-straw action in terms of marine pollution reduction.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; many customers disapprove of plastic straws in cafés.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; café straws account for around 5% of plastic items recovered from UK coastal cleanups, and banning them would directly cut this share.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; some customers with disabilities rely on flexible plastic straws to drink safely.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; discarded fishing gear is a larger source of marine plastic than café straws.

title: E-Scooter Helmet Law
stem: Should helmets be made legally mandatory for adults riding e-scooters to reduce serious head injuries?
answer_reason: C is the strongest: it connects helmets (the action) to serious head injuries (the outcome) with a specific published statistic. A addresses a narrow subgroup (commuters), not all adult riders. B appeals to a comparison with cycling rather than evidence on head injuries, and it relies on the unstated assumption that cycling rules imply the same benefit applies to e-scooters. D addresses ride frequency — not the outcome of serious head injuries.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; most commuters support the rule.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; cyclists are not legally required to wear helmets in the UK, so e-scooter riders should not be either.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a published hospital-admissions review found that e-scooter riders without helmets were around four times as likely to sustain a serious head injury as those wearing helmets.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; riders who have to carry a helmet may ride their scooters less often.

title: Longer Lunch Break
stem: Should office employees be given a one-hour lunch break, up from thirty minutes, to increase afternoon productivity?
answer_reason: A directly connects the longer break (the action) to afternoon productivity (the outcome) with a controlled trial — evidence-based and addressing both parts. B addresses worker happiness, a different outcome. C is a comparative deflection that does not argue against the productivity claim. D addresses working-hours policy generally rather than the action on the table.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a controlled trial at a similar-sized office found afternoon output rose by 8% when employees switched from a 30-minute to a 60-minute lunch break.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; workers who feel rested during the day are happier at work.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; early finishing times tend to improve afternoon productivity more than longer lunch breaks do.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; lengthening the lunch break would push the contracted working day out by thirty minutes for every employee.

title: Cashless Parking
stem: Should town-centre car parks switch to cashless-only payment to cut the cost of collecting and banking coins?
answer_reason: B addresses both the action (removing cash payment) and the outcome (cost of coin collection and banking) with a specific figure. A addresses a comparison with a different town but does not directly argue the cost reduction here. C addresses equity of access, a different outcome. D addresses payment speed rather than collection and banking costs.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a neighbouring town has already gone cashless.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; council records show that coin-handling and banking cost this car-park operator around £40,000 a year, all of which would be eliminated.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; some elderly drivers do not use smartphone apps or contactless cards and would struggle to park.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; paying by card can take longer than dropping a coin in a slot.

title: Garden Centre Survey
stem:
A garden centre surveys 120 customers about three purchase categories. 52 buy tools, 46 buy seeds, 40 buy plants. 18 buy tools and seeds, 14 buy tools and plants, 12 buy seeds and plants. 6 customers buy all three. 20 customers buy none of these three categories.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 6 buy all three and 20 buy none. Scan — B shows 8 in the centre, not 6 — eliminate B. C shows 18 outside, not 20 — eliminate C. That leaves A and D. The stem says 18 buy tools and seeds and 6 of those buy all three, so tools-and-seeds only = 18 − 6 = 12. A shows 12 there ✓. D shows 14 — eliminate D. Answer: A.

title: Drink Orders
stem:
A café logs 80 drink orders on a morning. 34 contain caffeine, 28 contain milk, 22 contain sugar. 12 contain both caffeine and milk, 8 contain both milk and sugar, 4 contain both caffeine and sugar. 2 drinks contain all three. 18 drinks contain none of these three.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 2 contain all three and 18 contain none. Scan — A shows 4 in the centre, not 2 — eliminate A. C shows 20 outside, not 18 — eliminate C. That leaves B and D. The stem says 4 drinks contain caffeine and sugar; in D the caffeine-and-sugar total is 6 + 2 = 8 — eliminate D. B matches every stated figure. Answer: B.

title: Community Centre Evenings
stem:
A community centre surveys 90 members about three evening activities. 35 attend yoga, 40 attend book club, 25 attend swimming. 10 members attend both yoga and book club. 12 members attend both book club and swimming. No member attends both yoga and swimming.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: the stem gives 10 in the yoga-and-book-club overlap and 12 in the book-club-and-swimming overlap. Scan — B shows 14 in the yoga-and-book-club overlap, not 10 — eliminate B. C shows 8 in the book-club-and-swimming overlap, not 12 — eliminate C. That leaves A and D. Yoga-only = 35 − 10 = 25; A shows 25 ✓, D shows 21 — eliminate D. Answer: A.

title: School Clubs
stem:
A school surveys 90 pupils about three after-school clubs. 28 attend debate, 30 attend drama, 26 attend coding. 14 pupils attend both debate and drama. No pupil attends both coding and debate. No pupil attends both coding and drama. 20 pupils attend none of these three clubs.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 20 pupils are outside all three and 14 attend both debate and drama. Scan — A shows 22 outside, not 20 — eliminate A. C shows 16 outside, not 20 — eliminate C. That leaves B and D. The stem says 14 attend both debate and drama; D shows 10 in that overlap — eliminate D. B matches every stated overlap and the none count. Answer: B.

title: Parcel Handling Tags
stem:
A delivery company tracks 120 parcels by the handling tags applied. 40 parcels are tagged fragile, 35 heavy, 30 dimensional, 25 return-to-sender. Some parcels have both fragile and heavy tags; some have both heavy and dimensional; some have both dimensional and return-to-sender. No other tag combinations occur. 12 parcels are tagged fragile and heavy, 10 are tagged heavy and dimensional, 8 are tagged dimensional and return-to-sender. 20 parcels have no handling tag.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: the three stated pair totals are 12 (fragile-heavy), 10 (heavy-dimensional) and 8 (dimensional-return), and 20 parcels have no tag. Scan — B shows 16 in the fragile-heavy overlap, not 12 — eliminate B. C shows 24 outside, not 20 — eliminate C. That leaves A and D. The stem says heavy-and-dimensional = 10; D shows 14 — eliminate D. Answer: A.

title: Community Programme Pairs
stem:
A community hub runs four programmes: yoga, choir, chess and pottery. 120 residents take part in total. Some residents attend both yoga and choir. Some residents attend both chess and pottery. No resident attends any other combination of these programmes. 30 attend yoga only, 25 attend choir only, 20 attend chess only, 15 attend pottery only. 18 attend both yoga and choir, 12 attend both chess and pottery.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 18 residents in the yoga-choir overlap and 12 in the chess-pottery overlap. Scan — B shows 14 in the yoga-choir overlap, not 18 — eliminate B. C shows 10 in the chess-pottery overlap, not 12 — eliminate C. That leaves A and D. The stem says 30 attend yoga only; D shows 28 — eliminate D. A has every stated figure and sums to 120. Answer: A.

title: Company Benefits Hub
stem:
The diagram shows 180 employees categorised by which benefits they have taken up. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents an employee who is on the benefits hub and has taken up the gym benefit but no other benefit?
answer_reason: The question asks for someone inside the hub and the gym, and outside every other benefit. Letter P is in the hub only, no gym. Letter Q is in the hub and cycle-to-work. Letter R is in the hub and dental. Letter T is in the hub and childcare. Letter S is in the hub and gym, and outside every other benefit — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter S.

title: Library Cycle
stem:
The diagram shows 240 library items categorised by which of five consecutive workflow stages they are currently in. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents an item that is currently in both the catalogued and the shelved stages, but is not in any other stage?
answer_reason: The question asks for an item inside catalogued and shelved and outside every other stage. Letter P is received only. Letter Q is received and catalogued. Letter S is shelved and borrowed — includes borrowed, which must be excluded. Letter R sits inside catalogued and shelved and outside every other stage — that matches. Answer: Letter R.

title: Wellness Activities Cycle
stem:
The diagram shows 140 staff categorised by which of four wellness activities they attend. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a member of staff who attends the yoga and meditation sessions only?
answer_reason: The question asks for staff in the yoga and meditation regions, and outside every other activity. Letter P is yoga only. Letter U is in the meditation and running overlap. Letter W is in the yoga and swimming overlap. Letter T is the yoga and meditation overlap and outside running and swimming — that matches. Answer: Letter T.

title: Clinic Check Hub
stem:
The diagram shows 200 clinic patients categorised by which of five health checks they have completed. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a patient who is registered and has completed the blood-pressure check but no other check?
answer_reason: The question asks for a patient inside the registered and blood-pressure regions and outside every other check. Letter P is registered only — no blood-pressure check. Letter R is registered and weight, not blood pressure. Letter T is registered and hearing, not blood pressure. Letter Q is registered and blood pressure and outside every other check — that matches. Answer: Letter Q.

title: Blood Pressure Monitors
stem:
Two home blood-pressure monitors are tested against a clinical reference. Monitor A gives the correct reading in 80 out of 100 tests. Monitor B gives the correct reading in 94 out of 100 tests. When each monitor is used to re-test the same arm 50 times in a row, Monitor A returns the same reading 48 times and Monitor B returns the same reading 39 times.

Which statement best compares the two monitors?
answer_reason: Accuracy = how often the reading is correct. Monitor A = 80%, Monitor B = 94% — B is more accurate. Precision = how consistent repeated readings are. Monitor A = 48/50 = 96%, Monitor B = 39/50 = 78% — A is more precise. So Monitor B is more accurate but Monitor A is more precise.

title: Coloured Tokens
stem:
A bag contains 6 red tokens, 5 yellow tokens and 4 black tokens. Two tokens are drawn at random, one after the other, without replacement.

What is the probability that both tokens are yellow?
answer_reason: Total tokens = 15. P(first yellow) = 5/15 = 1/3. After one yellow is removed, 4 yellow remain in 14 tokens. P(second yellow given first yellow) = 4/14 = 2/7. P(both yellow) = (1/3) × (2/7) = 2/21.

title: Rare Allergy Screen
stem:
A food allergy affects 1 in 500 adults. A screening test correctly identifies 98% of adults who have the allergy and correctly identifies 95% of adults who do not. An adult tests positive.

Approximately what is the probability that this adult actually has the allergy?
answer_reason: Consider 50,000 adults: 100 have the allergy, 49,900 do not. True positives = 98% of 100 = 98. False positives = 5% of 49,900 = 2,495. Total positives = 98 + 2,495 = 2,593. Probability of having the allergy given a positive test = 98 / 2,593 ≈ 0.038, so around 4%.

title: Biased Coins
stem:
A biased coin lands on heads with probability 0.6 on each toss, independently of previous tosses. The coin is tossed three times.

What is the probability of getting exactly two heads in the three tosses?
answer_reason: There are three sequences with exactly two heads (HHT, HTH, THH). Each has probability 0.6 × 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.144. Total probability = 3 × 0.144 = 0.432.

title: Hospital Theatre Roster
stem: All cardiac surgeries at the hospital must be performed in Theatre A unless the patient is under sixteen years old. Some cardiac surgeons are also trained in transplant surgery. No theatre nurse is permitted to administer an anaesthetic. Some anaesthetics in Theatre A are administered by trainee anaesthetists.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: An adult cardiac surgery may take place in Theatre B.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All adult cardiac surgeries must be in Theatre A; only patients under sixteen are exempt from that rule.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some transplant-trained doctors are cardiac surgeons.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some cardiac surgeons are transplant-trained, so by the same overlap some transplant-trained doctors are cardiac surgeons.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No theatre nurse can administer an anaesthetic in Theatre A.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Theatre nurses cannot administer an anaesthetic anywhere, so that includes Theatre A.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All anaesthetics in Theatre A are administered by trainee anaesthetists.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premises say only some are. Going from some to all is a quantifier shift.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a patient is fifteen, their cardiac surgery may be performed outside Theatre A.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: A fifteen-year-old is under sixteen, which triggers the unless exception, so the Theatre A requirement does not apply.

title: Vorms and Trels
stem: All vorms are trels. No trel is a glink. Some sloons are vorms. Most glinks are quemps.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No vorm is a glink.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All vorms are trels and no trel is a glink, so no vorm can be a glink.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some sloons are trels.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some sloons are vorms and all vorms are trels, so those sloons must also be trels.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All glinks are quemps.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Most glinks are quemps but most is not all. Going from most to all is a quantifier shift.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some quemps are not glinks.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: We only know that most glinks are quemps. Nothing is said about quemps that are not glinks, so we cannot deduce this.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some trels are glinks.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: No trel is a glink, so this directly contradicts the premise.

title: Greenhouse Plants
stem: Tropical plants in the nursery cannot survive without daily heating. All plants in the heated greenhouse receive daily heating. Some seedlings in the heated greenhouse are tropical plants. No cactus needs daily heating.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Tropical seedlings in the heated greenhouse are receiving the heating they need to survive.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Tropical plants need daily heating to survive, and every plant in the heated greenhouse receives daily heating, so tropical seedlings there are getting what they need.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All cacti in the heated greenhouse will die.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Cacti do not need daily heating, but the premises do not say they cannot tolerate it. We cannot conclude they will die.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every plant that receives daily heating is tropical.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premise is that tropical plants need daily heating, not that only tropical plants do. This is a reverse inference.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some plants in the heated greenhouse are not tropical.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some seedlings in the heated greenhouse are tropical, which under UCAT means more than zero but less than all, so some seedlings there are non-tropical.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a plant cannot survive without daily heating, it must be tropical.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Tropical plants need daily heating, but other plants might also need it. The reverse direction is not justified.

title: Software Patches
stem: If a software patch passes the security review, then it is released to production. All patches released to production are logged in the audit register. Some patches that fail the security review are still released to staging. No patch in staging is logged in the audit register.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every patch that passes the security review is logged in the audit register.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Passing the review means a patch is released to production, and every production release is logged. So passing implies logged.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some patches in staging have failed the security review.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some failed patches are released to staging, so among the patches in staging there are some that have failed.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All patches that fail the security review are released to staging.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premise only says some failed patches are released to staging. Going from some to all is a quantifier shift.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a patch is logged in the audit register, it must have passed the security review.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: We know passing leads to production and production leads to being logged, but the reverse direction is not given. A patch could be logged through some other route.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No patch released to production is in staging.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Production patches are logged, and no staging patch is logged, so no production patch can also be in staging.

title: Distinction Necessary
stem: Achieving a distinction in the chemistry exam is necessary to qualify for the advanced cohort. A grade of 80% or above on the exam is sufficient to be awarded a distinction. Most candidates who study with a tutor score above 80%. No candidate who fails the practical assessment can join the advanced cohort.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every candidate in the advanced cohort has achieved a distinction.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: A distinction is necessary to qualify for the advanced cohort, so every cohort member must have achieved one.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every candidate who scores 80% on the chemistry exam will join the advanced cohort.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Scoring 80% guarantees a distinction, but a distinction is only necessary, not sufficient, for the cohort. They could still be excluded for failing the practical, for example.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Most candidates who study with a tutor have achieved a distinction.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Most tutored candidates score above 80%, and scoring above 80% is sufficient for a distinction, so most tutored candidates have a distinction.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Anyone who has not achieved a distinction has failed the practical assessment.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Failing the practical is one way to be excluded from the cohort, but missing a distinction is not the same thing as failing the practical. The two are independent prerequisites.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a candidate joined the advanced cohort, they passed the practical assessment.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Failing the practical excludes a candidate from the cohort, so any cohort member must have passed the practical.

title: Coffee Tasting Order
stem:
Five samples of coffee — Bolivar, Castro, Dorian, Ember and Faro — are tasted in five rounds (1 to 5). Faro is tasted in round 1. Ember is tasted in round 2. Castro is tasted immediately after Dorian. Bolivar is tasted in a later round than Castro.

Which of the following lists the samples in tasting order from round 1 to round 5?
answer_reason: Faro = round 1 and Ember = round 2 are fixed, so rounds 3, 4 and 5 are split between Bolivar, Castro and Dorian. Castro is immediately after Dorian, so they sit at (3, 4) or (4, 5). If Dorian = 4 and Castro = 5, Bolivar would need to be later than 5, which is impossible. So Dorian = 3 and Castro = 4, leaving Bolivar = 5. Order: Faro, Ember, Dorian, Castro, Bolivar.

title: Restaurant Bills
stem:
A group of five diners — Anya, Bo, Cal, Devi and Eve — split the cost of their meal. The mean cost per diner is £20. Anya's bill is £4 more than Bo's. Bo's bill is £2 more than Cal's. Devi's bill is £4 more than Cal's. Eve's bill is £8 less than Anya's.

How much did Anya pay?
answer_reason: Total = 5 × £20 = £100. Let Cal's bill = C. Then Bo = C + 2, Anya = Bo + 4 = C + 6, Devi = C + 4 and Eve = Anya − 8 = C − 2. Sum = (C+6) + (C+2) + C + (C+4) + (C−2) = 5C + 10 = 100, so C = 18. Anya = 18 + 6 = £24.

title: Bookshelf Order
stem:
Six identical-looking books — labelled P, Q, R, S, T and U — are arranged on a shelf in positions 1 to 6 from left to right. T is in position 1. R is immediately to the left of P. P is to the right of Q. S is somewhere to the left of R. U is to the right of P.

Which book is in position 4?
answer_reason: T is fixed in position 1. R must sit immediately to the left of P, so they take two adjacent positions. U is to the right of P, so U occupies a position later than P. Try R = 4 and P = 5: then U = 6, leaving positions 2 and 3 for S and Q (S left of R and Q left of P are both satisfied either way). Other R-P pairings fail: R = 2, P = 3 leaves no later spot for U past 6; R = 3, P = 4 leaves no left-of-R spot for S that does not clash with T; R = 5, P = 6 leaves no later spot for U. So R is in position 4.

title: Festival Camping Plots
stem:
Six tents are arranged on a 2-row by 3-column grid (positions 1 to 3 in the top row, positions 4 to 6 in the bottom row). Hari's tent is directly above Joel's. Mira is in position 4 (the bottom-left corner). Naveen is to the immediate right of Mira. Owen is in the same row as Hari. Pia takes the remaining tent.

Which two people are guaranteed to be in the same column as each other?
answer_reason: Mira is in position 4 and Naveen in position 5. Hari sits directly above Joel, so Hari is in the top row and Joel is in the bottom row in the same column. Joel cannot be position 4 (Mira) or position 5 (Naveen), so Joel = 6 and Hari = 3. Owen is in the same row as Hari, so Owen is in the top row (position 1 or 2), and Pia takes the other top-row spot. Hari and Joel are always in column 3 together. Owen versus Naveen and Pia versus Mira each depend on which top-row spot Owen and Pia take, so they are not guaranteed.

title: Office Allocation
stem:
A small firm has four staff — Reza, Salma, Toby and Una — who must each be assigned to exactly one of four offices labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4. Una takes office 3. Toby's office number is no greater than 2. Salma's office number is greater than Toby's. Reza takes an office with a lower number than Toby's.

Which of the following is the correct office assignment?
answer_reason: Una = 3. Toby is in office 1 or 2. If Toby = 1, then Reza must be lower than 1, which is impossible, so Toby = 2. Reza < 2 means Reza = 1. The only office left for Salma is 4, which satisfies Salma > Toby. So the unique assignment is Reza in 1, Toby in 2, Una in 3, Salma in 4.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Reza in 1, Toby in 2, Una in 3, Salma in 4
